title: How rare is a page with 1,000 links?
hook: Most pages have a few links. Do pages with 1,000 links exist at all?

knows: most pages have few links, a few have many
doesNotKnow: that in a power law with exponent 2, ten times the links makes a page 100 times rarer at every scale, a straight line on log–log axes

misconception: Pages with 1,000 links are so rare they effectively don't exist, as in a bell curve.
objective: The learner can explain that when the share of pages with k links falls like 1/k², every tenfold step in k makes pages 100 times rarer, so the log–log plot is a straight line of slope −2 and pages with 1,000 links are rare but real.

claims.text: If the share of pages with k links is proportional to 1/k², pages with 1,000 links are 100 times rarer than pages with 100, and those are 100 times rarer than pages with 10.
claims.source: (1/100²)/(1/1,000²) = 100 and (1/10²)/(1/100²) = 100; in general (k/10)^-2 / k^-2 = 100 for every k. Matches the brief's check (ratio100vs1000 = 100). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. (1/100^2)/(1/1000^2) = 100 and (1/10^2)/(1/100^2) = 100. Chapter placement easley-kleinberg-2010 ch. 18 ('Power Laws and Rich-Get-Richer Phenomena') is right from my knowledge of the book; not opened (host blocked).

claims.text: On log–log axes this is a straight line of slope −2: down two powers of ten for every power of ten across.
claims.source: log10(c·k^-2) = log10 c − 2·log10 k, linear in log10 k with slope −2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. log10(c k^-2) = log10 c - 2 log10 k.

claims.text: On linear axes everything past about 10 links looks like zero, but there is no cliff: pages with 1,000 links are rare, not absent.
claims.source: Relative to k = 1 the share at k = 10 is 0.01 (about 1.6 px of the stage's 158 px chart height) and at k = 1,000 is 10^-6. A power-law share k^-2 stays positive and falls by the same factor per decade, whereas a bell-curve tail falls faster than any power of k. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): verified. On the stage's linear axes (k 0..1000 over 258 px, share over 158 px), k = 10 is 2.6 px right of the axis and 1.6 px up; k^-2 > 0 for all k.

recall.question: The share of pages with k links falls like 1/k². Pages with 10 links are how much more common than pages with 1,000?
recall.why: Two tenfold steps (10 → 100 → 1,000), each a factor of 100: 100 × 100 = 10,000.
